messages: emma (docs): FYI I'm hitting an odd class of broken links in the migration previews: anchors that include special characters (percent-encoded spaces, parentheses in example titles) are being normalized differently between MkDocs and Docusaurus. linkcheck flags them as missing. aj (devex): can you give a concrete failing example? encoded chars can be tricky in URLs vs HTML ids. emma (docs): sure. in `docs/guides/quickstart.md` we link to `/examples/python#setup (basic)` (note the space+parens). MkDocs produced `#setup-basic` whereas the docusaurus build made `#setup-%28basic%29` and the linkcheck in CI sees the old-style anchor and 404s. curl to preview: `curl -I https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/examples/python#setup (basic)` returns 200 for page but linkcheck cares about the fragment. pavan (eng): interesting. some slugify libs percent-encode reserved chars, others strip or replace them. We need to pick a canonical transform and emit compatibility mappings for the rest. lila (i18n): note: translated titles sometimes include punctuation that gets removed or encoded differently depending on locale. any transform must be applied consistently to localized slugs, or we'll end up with per-locale collisions. ci-bot: linkcheck: ERROR: broken fragment at /guides/quickstart -> target /examples/python#setup%20(basic) resolved to /examples/python#setup-basic (no match) 16. build step docs/linkcheck failed. emma (docs): proposal: 1) adopt a canonical slug strategy: percent-encode only when necessary, otherwise replace non-alnum with hyphens (kebab). 2) add a post-build pass that generates a small `redirects-fragments.json` mapping legacy-variant -> canonical for affected pages. 3) add a docs-lint rule to flag headings that contain parentheses/spaces so authors can prefer explicit ids: `## Setup (basic) {#setup-basic}`. aj (devex): I can hook in a custom slugifier for Docusaurus that mirrors MkDocs' python-slugify behavior (replace non-letter/number with hyphen, collapse repeats, trim). That should make the generated ids match most existing anchors. For rarer cases we'll generate the redirect map. pavan (eng): I'll write a tiny post-build comparer: parse all source headings, generate both MkDocs-style and Docusaurus-style slugs, diff them, and emit redirects only where they differ. Keep the list minimal. lila (i18n): I'll run the comparer across `i18n/*/docs` and produce a CSV of locales/pages impacted so translators can add explicit `{#id}` where appropriate. emma (docs): small nuance: image anchors (e.g., `![diagram](../assets/flow.png#diagram-1)`) are losing the fragment in the published HTML because the markdown renderer treats the hash as part of the image URL, not a fragment anchor. CI flagged a couple of these. aj (devex): yeah images with `#` in the filename or fragment are flaky. We should avoid fragment anchors on image URLs; instead add a nearby heading with explicit id and link to that. For now we can rewrite image links post-build to separate the fragment and ensure an `id` exists on a wrapping figure or caption. pavan (eng): agree. post-build repair will look for `` and move `id` to `
